criteria.name: Mission concept and rationale — What will it do, who are the users, why is it needed?
criteria.reasoning: Clear goals, function, users and Australian need identified with literature links. Objectives for SST, thermal stress, bathymetry and colour detection stated. Requirements lack quantified performance.

evidence.quote: A near-real-time relay to monitoring stations on the ground would allow marine

criteria.name: Project plan — How you plan to complete the assignment, including either a Gantt chart or a timetable and information sources you plan to use
criteria.reasoning: Gantt with weekly tasks, deadlines and staged STK work shows feasibility. No contingency provision, weak linkage of why sequence suits mission, and no explicit future information-source list.

criteria.name: Preliminary progress — Technical content and evidence of sufficient work done to date
criteria.reasoning: No results, plots, calculations or interpretation presented. Tutorials claimed without evidence. Major orbit error indicates not on track technically.

criteria.name: Report presentation
criteria.reasoning: Logical structure, readable writing, consistent formatting, labelled Gantt. Footnote URLs match superscripts but lack formal reference style and in-text citation consistency.

technical_issues.issue: States geostationary orbit at 600 km altitude: physically impossible, GEO is ~35786 km; 600 km is LEO and cannot be fixed above reef.

overall: Promising reef-monitoring concept with good rationale and usable plan, but no technical results and critical orbit misconception undermine readiness for full design.

feedback.summary: You made promising progress on your reef-monitoring mission with good rationale and a usable plan. Your report is well presented but lacks technical results and contains a critical orbit misconception to fix before full design.
next_steps: Correct your orbit baseline in Project Plan & Preliminary Progress: 600 km is LEO, not geostationary, and cannot stay fixed above the reef.
Add quantified requirements and a contingency-linked plan with explicit future information sources to strengthen your mission narrative.
Include brief interpreted preliminary results, plots or calculations with formal citations to show you are on track.

criteria.C1: In Mission Concept & Rationale you clearly linked SST, thermal stress, bathymetry and colour detection to Australian reef users and need, with literature links. Well done. To strengthen within Accomplished, you need quantified performance requirements for each objective, such as resolution, accuracy, revisit and latency targets tied to user needs.
criteria.C2: Your Image 1 Gantt with weekly tasks, deadlines and staged STK work in Project Plan & Preliminary Progress shows feasibility. To reach Accomplished you need contingency for variations, explain why the sequence fits your reef mission narrative, and list explicit future information sources with references.
criteria.C3: In Project Plan & Preliminary Progress you stated completed STK tutorials 1-4 but included no results, plots or calculations. You also described geostationary orbit at 600 km, which cannot stay fixed above the reef. To reach Adequate you need brief interpreted results and correct orbit basics to show you are on track.
criteria.C4: Your Mission Concept & Rationale and labelled Gantt follow logical structure with readable writing and consistent formatting. Well done. To consolidate Accomplished you need formal reference style with consistent in-text citations where text matches list, instead of footnote URLs only.
